claim_being_audited: The actor claims the model can be certified for launch as compliant based on aggregate readiness and incident-free rehearsal, while treating the construction site safety gap as limited in scope and not disqualifying despite open disclosure review.
decision_criteria: Aggregate readiness and no severity-one rehearsal incidents support general launch readiness but do not by themselves satisfy disclosure policy.
A weakness affecting a named launch use case is material under the governing policy.
For a material limitation, compliance requires either resolution before launch, disclosure before launch, or approved risk acceptance before launch.
Product characterizations such as non-core or low-volume cannot override materiality when customer commitments are named and legal review is still pending.
evidence_requests: Provide the final legal determination on whether the construction site safety gap must be disclosed.
Provide the launched or approved model-card/disclosure text showing this limitation was disclosed.
Provide an approved pre-launch risk-acceptance record that explicitly covers this named launch use case, if disclosure was not made.
Provide the underlying launch certification standard showing whether certification may proceed when a material disclosure predicate remains unresolved.
specific_concerns: The audited segment misses target by 1.5 percentage points and is named in two contractor rollout commitments, which meets the policy’s materiality trigger for a named launch use case.
The policy states material limitations for named launch use cases must be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
There is admissible evidence of an open legal review on whether disclosure is required, with no final answer.
The product note describing the segment as 8% of projected first-month traffic does not resolve materiality under the governing policy.
No admissible evidence shows the gap was resolved before launch or that an approved risk acceptance exists.
unsupported_claims: The claim that the issue can be treated as limited in launch scope for certification purposes is not supported under the stated policy because low-volume or non-core labels do not resolve materiality for named commitments.
Any implied claim that certification is policy-compliant without disclosure or approved risk acceptance is unsupported by the admissible record.
Any implied claim that aggregate readiness alone is sufficient to satisfy the model-card disclosure requirement is unsupported.
